changed.from: There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\) one can construct at least \(c_0a_n^{-1}\) separated centers on the canonical trimmed straight boundary and a corresponding finite family of laws in \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}\) with the following properties. Every boundary is straight, every assignment is the two-half-plane partition, every \(\mu_{t,P}\) in the hard family is affine, every \(f_P\) is continuous and remains between the same fixed density bounds, and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common. The target curves are separated by at least \(c_1a_n\) in sup norm, while each relevant compressed product law obeys a Kullback--Leibler bound at most \(\alpha\log(c_0a_n^{-1})\) against the packing center. The density perturbations use \(\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}\), vary angular imbalance at radial scale \(a_n\), and preserve the radial mass envelope.
changed.to:
There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The assignment interface is straight; the regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), their arm-specific radial laws at \(x_j\) agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) and preserve every arm-specific radial mass density.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).
changed.reason: The frozen affine and center-count clauses are incompatible with a many-coordinate H"older packing when \(q>1\).  In addition, on the canonical square at \(L=4\), the lower density bound and normalization force the density to be uniform, leaving no angular-density perturbation.  The proposed statement records the construction actually proved and retains the logarithmic divergence budget needed by the frontier theorems.

changed.from: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\). changed.to:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  On the nonempty canonical class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\),
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), then the density envelope and the fixed square support force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently the distance and location exponents are strictly separated for \(q>1\) when \(L>4\), while they coincide when \(q=1\) and also throughout the no-density-slack boundary case \(L=4\).
changed.reason: At \(L=4\), integration of the lower density envelope over the fixed area-four square forces \(f_P\equiv1/4\).  The distance radial regression then inherits the order-\(q\) Taylor remainder and has the faster rate, so the frozen all-\(L\) first-order lower bound is false.  Strict density slack \(L>4\) is exactly the regime in which the proved angular construction lies in the canonical straight class.

Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\), and let \(Z_0\) be ancillary.  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
\Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
\leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

directive:
D0.5 BOUNDARY REPAIR — implement all findings atomically without strengthening assumptions or changing the estimand.

1. Repair thm:angular-remainder-transition. Preserve the order-m joint normalized-coarea upper bound for every 1 <= m <= min(q,iota). The written width-h, height-c h^m bump converse is not H^q-compatible when m<q because its q-th derivatives scale as h^(m-q). Restrict the explicit matching bump converse to the valid m=q case (and only subclasses containing that uniform-design straight-interface q-Hölder bump submodel). For m<q, state only the proved upper rate unless a genuinely H^q-compatible same-rate construction is derived; do not use a vacuous containment premise to certify the invalid witness. Synchronize the theorem, proof, comparator table, tldr, honest scope, and all prose that currently suggests exactness for arbitrary m.

2. Promote the stabilized coordinatewise degree-(m-1) local-polynomial estimator, including Gram matrix, outcome vector, eigenvalue cutoff, zero convention, arm difference, bandwidth domain, and decision-class measurability, into a typed definition/theorem-level deliverable. The angular-transition theorem must depend on and cite that definition; proof text may then invoke it rather than being its sole location.

3. Repair both exceptional-event arguments in thm:angular-remainder-transition and thm:straight-information-gap. Failure of the concentration event does not imply cutoff failure. On cutoff-active outcomes, use the cutoff-controlled inverse together with explicit bounds on the empirical outcome vector and the conditional sub-Gaussian envelope (plus the polynomially small concentration-complement probability) to bound the exceptional contribution. On cutoff-fail outcomes the estimator is zero and the bounded target controls loss. State the moment calculation explicitly; never claim the estimator is automatically zero on the entire concentration complement.

4. Remove ass:boundary-length-envelope from def:rectifiable-class membership, thm:rectifiable-exact-frontier dependencies, and all reverse-use/usage metadata because neither bound uses it: the upper cover is supplied by the ambient compact square and the lower family already satisfies the enlarged class. Retain the assumption only where independently used by another class, if any. Synchronize the rectifiable theorem and prose to the enlarged primitive two-sided-thickness class without advertising this routine cleanup as a new headline.

Preserve the exact a_n rectifiable and smooth-saturation frontiers, the L>4/L=4 straight information elbow, the angular-density packing, direct-product lemma, all law envelopes except deletion of the inert rectifiable boundary-length membership, and every prior no-same-class-CTY disclaimer. Make no new assumption and do not enter F.

There is no density-only weakest regularity threshold for the faster distance frontier.  The operational threshold is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix an integer \(m\) with \(1\leq m\leq\min\{q,\iota\}\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
for coefficient functions uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Then the explicit coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) local-polynomial estimator with bandwidth \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2m+2)}\) obeys
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)\leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(\mathcal C\) contains the uniform-design, straight-interface H\"older bump submodel of order \(m\), the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  In contrast, any class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus \(m=1\) is first-order saturation and every \(m\geq2\) gives a faster geometry-sensitive frontier.  A condition on \(f_P\) alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for the order: the normalized product integrals \(N/Q\), rather than the density in isolation, are the minimal operational objects.

The operational upper condition is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix an integer \(m\) with \(1\leq m\leq\min\{q,\iota\}\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), using the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m=q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^q\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted here when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields a faster geometry-sensitive upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate supplied here applies exactly at \(m=q\).  A condition on \(f_P\) alone is neither necessary nor sufficient to determine the order: the normalized product integrals \(N/Q\), rather than the density in isolation, are the operational objects.
changed.reason: For \(m<q\), a width-\(h\), height-\(h^m\) bump has a \(q\)-th derivative of order \(h^{m-q}\) and is not contained in the frozen \(q\)-H\"older class.  The upper theorem remains valid for every admissible \(m\), while the explicit bump converse is valid at \(m=q\).

{"id":"def:stabilized-distance-local-polynomial","name":"\widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}","construction":"Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), a cutoff constant \(c>0\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Put \(v_m(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{m-1})^\top\), let \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), and set \(S_{P,x,i}=|D_{P,x,i}|\).  At the probability-zero value \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), assign the observation to neither arm.  Define
\[
 \widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
Let
\[
 G_m=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad \lambda_m(c)=c\lambda_{\min}(G_m),
\]
and define the stabilized arm intercept and arm difference by
\[
 \widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h),
 &\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}\geq\lambda_m(c)/2,\\
 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}<\lambda_m(c)/2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{1,h,c}(x)
 -\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{0,h,c}(x).
\]
The cutoff input \(c\) is suppressed from the notation for \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\).  The formula is defined for every \(h>0\); in an order-\(m\) coarea class it is used with \(c=\underline c\) and \(0<h\leq r_*\).  The strict sign convention, eigenvalue cutoff, inverse branch, and zero branch make this a pointwise Borel formula of \(U_{n,P}(x)\).","free_symbols":["m","n","t","h","P","Y","\mathcal{B}_P","D_{P,x}","U_{n,P}(x)","K_\triangle","\widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}"],"inputs":["def:distance-data","def:distance-decision-class","def:triangular-kernel"]}

There is no density-only weakest regularity threshold for the faster distance frontier.  The operational upper condition is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix an integer \(m\) with \(1\leq m\leq\min\{q,\iota\}\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), using the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m=q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^q\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted here when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields a faster geometry-sensitive upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate supplied here applies exactly at \(m=q\).  A condition on \(f_P\) alone is neither necessary nor sufficient to determine the order: the normalized product integrals \(N/Q\), rather than the density in isolation, are the operational objects.

changed.to:
The operational sufficient condition for a faster coordinatewise-distance frontier is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix any integer \(m\geq1\), with ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), built with \(K_\triangle\) and the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields the faster displayed upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate applies for every fixed \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that a locally constant regression gives \(N(s)/Q(s)\) equal to that constant at every sufficiently small radius, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives \(N(s)/Q(s)=s^{1+\alpha}/2\) on the treated half-circle for some \(0<\alpha<1\), and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder.  Hence density alone does not determine these examples' joint normalized-coarea remainder; no universal weakest-threshold impossibility is asserted.

\(h^{2q}h^2\), so the product relative entropy is at most \(Cnh^{2q+2}\). \[

\]
whereas any decoder with error probability \(p_e\) satisfies
\(I(J;Z)\geq(1-p_e)\log M-\log2\).  Hence \(p_e\) is bounded away from zero.  Sup-norm accuracy smaller than half the bump height would decode \(J\), proving the lower bound \(cs_{n,q}\).  This lower bound applies even to the full-location class, and therefore also to the distance-only class.

\[
 1=\int_{[-1,1]^2}f_P(z)\,dz\geq1.
\]
Equality forces \(f_P=1/4\) almost everywhere, and continuity makes the equality pointwise.  For a trimmed boundary point and sufficiently small \(s\), each arm-specific half-circle lies inside the square, so \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\pi s/4\).  Taylor's formula for \(\mu_{t,P}\), integrated over that half-circle, gives coefficients \(b_{t,k,P}(x)\) such that

A degree-\((q-1)\) one-sided local polynomial in signed radius therefore has bias \(Ch^q\), denominator order \(nh^2\), and uniform stochastic term \(C\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\).  Balancing gives the distance upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\).  The full-location lower bound already proved transfers to the smaller distance decision class, so the distance lower bound is \(cs_{n,q}\). {"id":"thm:angular-remainder-transition","kind":"theorem","statement":"The operational sufficient condition for a faster coordinatewise-distance frontier is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry. \[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), built with \(K_\triangle\) and the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields the faster displayed upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate applies for every fixed \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that a locally constant regression gives \(N(s)/Q(s)\) equal to that constant at every sufficiently small radius, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives \(N(s)/Q(s)=s^{1+\alpha}/2\) on the treated half-circle for some \(0<\alpha<1\), and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder. {"id":"lem:angular-density-packing","kind":"lemma","statement":"There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The assignment interface is straight; the regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both arm-specific radial mass densities at \(x_j\) agree at every radius, their arm-specific radial laws at \(x_j\) agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and arm-specific local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).","free_symbols":["n","q","c_{-}","L","r_0","\delta","P","a_n","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}","\mu_{t,P}","f_P","\tau_P","\mathbb{Q}_{n,P,x}","\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}"],"depends_on":["ass:assignment-partition","ass:density-continuity","ass:density-envelope","ass:holder-regressions","ass:variance-envelope","ass:uniform-two-sided-thickness","ass:straight-half-plane-design","def:rectifiable-class","def:smooth-class","def:straight-class","def:frontier-rates","def:angular-density-handle"],"proof_tex":"We prove the narrowed statement and check all support, geometric, positivity, moment, and division conditions.

First use the unit square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), the lower and upper half-square assignment regions, and the interface
\[
\mathcal B=\{(u-1/2,0):0\leq u\leq1\},
\qquad \gamma(u)=(u-1/2,0).
\]
The base score density is \(f_*=1\).  The chart has length one, speed one, all derivatives of order at least two equal to zero, and \(C^{\iota+2}\)-norm at most one.  The line segment is closed and convex, hence every point in the plane has a unique metric projection onto it and its reach is infinite.  Thus the length, speed, derivative, and reach requirements hold for every \(L\geq4\), \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\rho_0>0\).  At an endpoint, the intersection of an arm and a sufficiently small boundary ball contains a quarter disk.  Since all densities constructed below are at least \(3/4\), for \(r\leq r_0\leq1/4\) each arm has mass at least \(3\pi r^2/16\), which exceeds \(c_{-}r^2\) because \(c_{-}\leq1/(16L)\).  Compact support and the assignment-partition conditions are immediate.

Choose a nonnegative radial \(C^\infty\) function \(\phi\), supported in the open unit disk, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  Put
\[
\Delta=d a_n,
\qquad
w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q},
\]
where the fixed constants are selected below.  Pack the interval \(\gamma([\delta,1-\delta])\) by centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) separated by at least \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the disks \(B_2(x_j,w)\) are disjoint and contained in the unit square at a positive distance from the chart endpoints, and elementary interval packing gives
\[
M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Let \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).  For every derivative order \(k\leq q\),
\[
\lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
\leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}
\leq C_\phi d_1^{-1}.
\]
Since the supports are disjoint, the same bound holds for every signed sum.  Taking \(d_1\) sufficiently large and the fixed affine slope \(b>0\) sufficiently small therefore puts all regressions below in the prescribed \(q\)-H\"older ball.

For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), define
\[
p_{0,\omega}(z)=\frac12,
\qquad
p_{1,\omega}(z)=\frac12+bz_1+\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
After decreasing \(b\) and \(d\), these functions take values in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), take independent variables
\[
Y(t)=B_t+\varepsilon_t,
\qquad
B_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{t,\omega}(z)),
\qquad
\varepsilon_t\sim N(0,1).
\]
Then \(\mu_{t,P_\omega}=p_{t,\omega}\) and
\(1\leq\sigma^2_{t,P_\omega}\leq5/4\), which lies in \([L^{-1},L]\).  Hoeffding's lemma and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[e^{\lambda\{Y(t)-p_{t,\omega}(X)\}}\mid X\right]
\leq e^{\lambda^2/8}e^{\lambda^2/2}
\leq e^{L^2\lambda^2/2},
\]
so the tail condition is uniform.

It remains to hide each regression bump in the radial experiment at its own center.  In polar coordinates \(z=x_j+r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), take a continuous cutoff \(\chi\) satisfying \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\) and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\), and set
\[
A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\phi(r/w)}{br}\,
\chi\!\left(\frac{br}{8\Delta}\right).
\]
There is no division at zero because the cutoff is identically zero on a neighborhood of zero.  On its active region \(br\geq8\Delta\), \(\lvert A_n(r)\rvert\leq1/4\), and smooth compact support of \(\phi\) makes the correction continuous at the outer edge.  Because the disks are disjoint, the formula
\[
f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_jA_n(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2)
\frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2}
\mathbf 1\{z\in B_2(x_j,w)\}
\]
is unambiguous, with the summand defined as zero at \(x_j\).  Its angular correction integrates to zero on every full circle, so \(\int_Sf_\omega=1\); it is continuous and belongs to \([3/4,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).

Now compare adjacent vertices \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{(j)}\).  On either half-circle centered at \(x_j\), \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta=0\).  Hence both arm-specific radial mass densities agree at \(x_j\) at every radius.  On the treated upper half-circle, whenever \(br\geq16\Delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega}(x_j+r e_\theta)\{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
-\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+r e_\theta)\,d\theta\\
&\qquad=\pi\Delta\phi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r)=0,
\end{aligned}
\]
after orienting the adjacent pair so that \(\omega_j=1\).  The control equality follows from its constant regression.  A Bernoulli variable followed by the common Gaussian channel is determined, after angular mixing at a fixed radius, by the averaged Bernoulli success probability.  Thus the entire arm-specific radial laws agree outside \(r\leq16\Delta/b\), not only their conditional means.

Inside this radius, the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), all Bernoulli probabilities remain in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their radially averaged success probabilities differ by at most \(C\Delta\).  The inequalities \(\log u\leq u-1\) and data processing through the common Gaussian channel give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(B+\varepsilon,B'+\varepsilon)\leq\operatorname{kl}(p,p').
\]
Consequently one compressed observation satisfies
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega,x_j},P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega^{(j)},x_j})
\leq C\int_0^{16\Delta/b}\Delta^2r\,dr
\leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Tensorization gives \(C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n\).  Moreover
\[
\log M=\left(\frac{1}{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choosing \(d\) sufficiently small gives the asserted bound for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\), with enough slack that Poissonization at mean \(2n\) still has exponent below \(1/4\).  At \(x_j\), the adjacent target curves differ by \(\Delta\phi_j(x_j)=d a_n\), so \(c_1=d\).  The global density bounds already proved, together with the fixed half-square geometry, give common upper and lower arm-mass envelopes over the entire hypercube.  This completes membership in both \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).

For the canonical square \([-1,1]^2\), use the required chart \(\gamma(u)=(2u-1,0)\) and base density \(f_*=1/4\).  When \(L>4\), let \(\varepsilon_L=1-4/L>0\), replace the cutoff constant \(8\) by a constant \(C_L\geq4/\varepsilon_L\), and choose \(d_1\) sufficiently large and then \(d/b\) sufficiently small as functions of \(L\).  The first choice keeps the cancellation region inside every bump also when \(q=1\); the second keeps its radius and all bump disks away from the trimmed endpoints for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The relative density perturbation is then at most \(\varepsilon_L/2\), so
\[
L^{-1}\leq\frac14(1-\varepsilon_L/2)\leq f_\omega

If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).","free_symbols":["n","q","c_{-}","L","r_0","\delta","P","a_n","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}","\mu_{t,P}","f_P","\tau_P","\mathbb{Q}_{n,P,x}","\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}"],"depends_on":["ass:assignment-partition","ass:score-absolute-continuity","ass:density-upper-envelope","ass:density-continuity","ass:density-envelope","ass:holder-regressions","ass:variance-envelope","ass:uniform-two-sided-thickness","ass:straight-half-plane-design","def:rectifiable-class","def:smooth-class","def:straight-class","def:frontier-rates","def:angular-density-handle"],"status":"proved","justification":"This explicit compressed-experiment construction converts angular-density confounding into the logarithmic uniform lower bound even under a straight interface and smooth regressions.","gap":"The published pointwise converse does not distribute continuous angular-density perturbations over separated trimmed-boundary centers with a logarithmic divergence budget.","consumer":"The rectifiable, smooth, and strict-slack straight-class distance converses use this contained stronger family.","proof_tex":"We prove the narrowed statement and check all support, geometric, positivity, moment, and division conditions.

First use the unit square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), the lower and upper half-square assignment regions, and the interface
\[
\mathcal B=\{(u-1/2,0):0\leq u\leq1\},
\qquad \gamma(u)=(u-1/2,0).
\]
The base score density is \(f_*=1\).  The chart has length one, speed one, all derivatives of order at least two equal to zero, and \(C^{\iota+2}\)-norm at most one.  The line segment is closed and convex, hence every point in the plane has a unique metric projection onto it and its reach is infinite.  Thus the length, speed, derivative, and reach requirements hold for every \(L\geq4\), \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\rho_0>0\).  At an endpoint, the intersection of an arm and a sufficiently small boundary ball contains a quarter disk. Choose a nonnegative radial \(C^\infty\) function \(\phi\), supported in the open unit disk, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  Put
\[
\Delta=d a_n,
\qquad
w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q},
\]
where the fixed constants are selected below.  Pack the interval \(\gamma([\delta,1-\delta])\) by centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) separated by at least \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the disks \(B_2(x_j,w)\) are disjoint and contained in the unit square at a positive distance from the chart endpoints, and elementary interval packing gives
\[
M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Let \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).  For every derivative order \(k\leq q\),
\[
\lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
\leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}
\leq C_\phi d_1^{-1}.
\]
Since the supports are disjoint, the same bound holds for every signed sum.  Taking \(d_1\) sufficiently large and the fixed affine slope \(b>0\) sufficiently small therefore puts all regressions below in the prescribed \(q\)-H\"older ball.

For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), define
\[
p_{0,\omega}(z)=\frac12,
\qquad
p_{1,\omega}(z)=\frac12+bz_1+\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
After decreasing \(b\) and \(d\), these functions take values in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), take independent variables
\[
Y(t)=B_t+\varepsilon_t,
\qquad
B_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{t,\omega}(z)),
\qquad
\varepsilon_t\sim N(0,1).
\]
Then \(\mu_{t,P_\omega}=p_{t,\omega}\) and
\(1\leq\sigma^2_{t,P_\omega}\leq5/4\), which lies in \([L^{-1},L]\).  Hoeffding's lemma and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[e^{\lambda\{Y(t)-p_{t,\omega}(X)\}}\mid X\right]
\leq e^{\lambda^2/8}e^{\lambda^2/2}
\leq e^{L^2\lambda^2/2},
\]
so the tail condition is uniform.

It remains to hide each regression bump in the radial experiment at its own center.  In polar coordinates \(z=x_j+r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), take a continuous cutoff \(\chi\) satisfying \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\) and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\), and set
\[
A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\phi(r/w)}{br}\,
\chi\!\left(\frac{br}{8\Delta}\right).
\]
There is no division at zero because the cutoff is identically zero on a neighborhood of zero.  On its active region \(br\geq8\Delta\), \(\lvert A_n(r)\rvert\leq1/4\), and smooth compact support of \(\phi\) makes the correction continuous at the outer edge.  Because the disks are disjoint, the formula
\[
f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_jA_n(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2)
\frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2}
\mathbf 1\{z\in B_2(x_j,w)\}
\]
is unambiguous, with the summand defined as zero at \(x_j\).  Its angular correction integrates to zero on every full circle, so \(\int_Sf_\omega=1\); it is continuous and belongs to \([3/4,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).

Now compare adjacent vertices \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{(j)}\).  On either half-circle centered at \(x_j\), \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta=0\).  Hence both arm-specific radial mass densities agree at \(x_j\) at every radius.  On the treated upper half-circle, whenever \(br\geq16\Delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega}(x_j+r e_\theta)\{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
-\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+r e_\theta)\,d\theta\\
&\qquad=\pi\Delta\phi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r)=0,
\end{aligned}
\]
after orienting the adjacent pair so that \(\omega_j=1\).  The control equality follows from its constant regression.  A Bernoulli variable followed by the common Gaussian channel is determined, after angular mixing at a fixed radius, by the averaged Bernoulli success probability.  Thus the entire arm-specific radial laws agree outside \(r\leq16\Delta/b\), not only their conditional means.

Inside this radius, the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), all Bernoulli probabilities remain in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their radially averaged success probabilities differ by at most \(C\Delta\).  The inequalities \(\log u\leq u-1\) and data processing through the common Gaussian channel give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(B+\varepsilon,B'+\varepsilon)\leq\operatorname{kl}(p,p').
\]
Consequently one compressed observation satisfies
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega,x_j},P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega^{(j)},x_j})
\leq C\int_0^{16\Delta/b}\Delta^2r\,dr
\leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Tensorization gives \(C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n\).  Moreover
\[

\]
Choosing \(d\) sufficiently small gives the asserted bound for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\), with enough slack that Poissonization at mean \(2n\) still has exponent below \(1/4\).  At \(x_j\), the adjacent target curves differ by \(\Delta\phi_j(x_j)=d a_n\), so \(c_1=d\).  The global density bounds already proved, together with the fixed half-square geometry, give common upper and lower arm-mass envelopes over the entire hypercube.  This completes membership in both \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).

For the canonical square \([-1,1]^2\), use the required chart \(\gamma(u)=(2u-1,0)\) and base density \(f_*=1/4\).  When \(L>4\), let \(\varepsilon_L=1-4/L>0\), replace the cutoff constant \(8\) by a constant \(C_L\geq4/\varepsilon_L\), and choose \(d_1\) sufficiently large and then \(d/b\) sufficiently small as functions of \(L\).  The first choice keeps the cancellation region inside every bump also when \(q=1\); the second keeps its radius and all bump disks away from the trimmed endpoints for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The relative density perturbation is then at most \(\varepsilon_L/2\), so
\[
L^{-1}\leq\frac14(1-\varepsilon_L/2)\leq f_\omega
\leq\frac14(1+\varepsilon_L/2)\leq L.
\]
The cancellation and divergence calculations are unchanged up to constants depending on \(L\).  This verifies the canonical-square clause for \(L>4\).  At \(L=4\), the lower envelope \(f\geq1/4\) on a square of area four and normalization force \(f\equiv1/4\), so no nonzero angular density perturbation is possible; no canonical-square claim is made in that boundary case."}

changed.to:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cup\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P\{T=t,\ \lVert X-x\rVert_2\leq r\}
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
 \geq c_-r^2,
 \qquad 0<r\leq r_0.
\]
Thus zero belongs to the essential support of each observed arm-specific radial measure.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
 =\mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s].
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls
\]
for \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\)-almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  Consequently the separate essential arm limit exists and satisfies
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x),
 \qquad
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]
No value at \(s=0\) or at a zero-denominator radius, and no radius sequence common to the two arms, is used.
changed.reason: Radon--Nikodym versions agree with circle integrals only almost everywhere, and a conditional regression is undefined where its radial density vanishes. The replacement states the valid observed-arm, essential-support, and separate-arm-limit result.

There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The assignment interface is straight; the regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both arm-specific radial mass densities at \(x_j\) agree at every radius, their arm-specific radial laws at \(x_j\) agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and arm-specific local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).

\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), then the density envelope and the fixed square support force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently the distance and location exponents are strictly separated for \(q>1\) when \(L>4\), while they coincide when \(q=1\) and also throughout the no-density-slack boundary case \(L=4\).

\[

\]
The location upper bound is attained by the named stabilized bivariate degree-\((q-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) from \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}location\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), with

\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), normalization, the density floor, and the fixed square support force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently, for \(q>1\), distance compression has the slower exponent in the strict-slack case \(L>4\); the exponents coincide when \(q=1\), and the no-slack normalization case \(L=4\) coincides for every \(q\).

changed.from:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), polar coarea gives, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 P\{X\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}=\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\), so the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) recovers the treatment arm almost surely.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]=\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
If, on some \((0,r_*]\), both arm denominators are positive and each ratio converges to \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) as \(s\downarrow0\), then
\[
 \tau_P(x)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\left\{\frac{N_{1,P,x}(s)}{Q_{1,P,x}(s)}-\frac{N_{0,P,x}(s)}{Q_{0,P,x}(s)}\right\}.
\]
changed.to:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the fixed observable radial Radon--Nikodym versions satisfy, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 P\{T=t,\ 0<\lVert X-x\rVert_2\leq r\}
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds,
\]
and agree with the corresponding observed-arm circle integrals for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\).  Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\), so the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) recovers the treatment arm almost surely.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
If zero lies in the essential support of each arm-specific radial measure and the two separate essential limits satisfy \(\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x)\), then
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)
 =\tau_P(x).
\]
In particular, the almost-everywhere radial lower bound and normalized-coarea remainder in \(\mathrm{thm:angular\text{-}remainder\text{-}transition}\) imply these premises arm by arm.
changed.reason: The ambient coarea class supplies observable radial Radon--Nikodym identities only almost everywhere; causal equality requires separate essential arm limits, not a pointwise positive interval or a common radius sequence.

changed.from:
The operational sufficient condition for a faster coordinatewise-distance frontier is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix any integer \(m\geq1\), with ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), built with \(K_\triangle\) and the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields the faster displayed upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate applies for every fixed \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that a locally constant regression gives \(N(s)/Q(s)\) equal to that constant at every sufficiently small radius, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives \(N(s)/Q(s)=s^{1+\alpha}/2\) on the treated half-circle for some \(0<\alpha<1\), and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder.  Hence density alone does not determine these examples' joint normalized-coarea remainder; no universal weakest-threshold impossibility is asserted.
changed.to:
Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  This is a conditional risk-transfer theorem.  Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be a subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
\]
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|
 \leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Under exactly these radial hypotheses, zero lies in the essential support of each observed radial measure, \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) equals \((0,r_*]\) modulo a Lebesgue-null set there, and the separate observed arm limits identify \(\tau_P(x)\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently, under those same radial hypotheses,
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If, in addition, \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains for every sufficiently large \(n\) the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted without that containment, and none is asserted for \(m<q\).  Independently, a law class that contains the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate only when the order-one radial hypotheses and that hard-family containment both hold; for every \(m\geq2\), the faster displayed upper rate is asserted only under the order-\(m\) radial hypotheses, and its matching converse additionally requires contained bumps and \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that, for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small treated-half-circle radius, a locally constant regression gives a constant normalized-coarea ratio, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives the ratio \(s^{1+\alpha}/2\) for some \(0<\alpha<1\) and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder even in the almost-everywhere sense.  Hence density alone does not determine these examples' joint normalized-coarea remainder; no universal weakest-threshold impossibility is asserted.
changed.reason: The theorem is a conditional transfer result. The radial inequalities and remainder hold only almost everywhere, every faster-rate conclusion is conditional on them, and exactness additionally requires a contained bump submodel with the stated smoothness boundary.

The observed arms are the two half-squares; the regressions are disjoint radial \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and actual-arm local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both observed arm-specific radial measures at \(x_j\) agree, their fixed Radon--Nikodym densities therefore agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere, their arm-specific radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and actual-arm local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).","free_symbols":["n","q","c_{-}","L","r_0","\delta","P","a_n","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}","\mu_{t,P}","f_P","\tau_P","\mathbb{Q}_{n,P,x}","\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}"],"depends_on":["ass:assignment-partition","ass:score-absolute-continuity","ass:density-upper-envelope","ass:density-continuity","ass:density-envelope","ass:holder-regressions","ass:variance-envelope","ass:uniform-two-sided-thickness","ass:straight-half-plane-design","def:rectifiable-class","def:smooth-class","def:straight-class","def:frontier-rates","def:angular-density-handle"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"This explicit compressed-experiment construction converts angular-density confounding into the logarithmic uniform lower bound even under a straight interface and smooth regressions.","gap":"The published pointwise converse does not distribute continuous angular-density perturbations over separated trimmed-boundary centers with a logarithmic divergence budget.","consumer":"The rectifiable, smooth, and strict-slack straight-class distance converses use this contained stronger family."}

\[
 P\{T=t,\ 0<\lVert X-x\rVert_2\leq r\}
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds,
\]
and agree with the corresponding observed-arm circle integrals for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\).  Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\), so the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) recovers the treatment arm almost surely.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
If zero lies in the essential support of each arm-specific radial measure and the two separate essential limits satisfy \(\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x)\), then
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)
 =\tau_P(x).
\]
In particular, the almost-everywhere radial lower bound and normalized-coarea remainder in \(\mathrm{thm:angular\text{-}remainder\text{-}transition}\) imply these premises arm by arm.","free_symbols":["P","q","\iota","L","t","X","Y","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{coarea}}","\mathcal{B}_P","\mathcal{A}_{0,P}","\mathcal{A}_{1,P}","Q_{t,P,x}","N_{t,P,x}","D_{P,x}","\mu_{t,P}","\tau_P"],"depends_on":["ass:deterministic-assignment","ass:consistency","ass:score-absolute-continuity","def:circle-density-integral","def:circle-outcome-integral","def:signed-distance","def:radial-coarea-ambient-class"],"status":"to-prove"}

changed.from:
{"id":"thm:angular-remainder-transition","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  This is a conditional risk-transfer theorem.  Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be a subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
\]
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|
 \leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Under exactly these radial hypotheses, zero lies in the essential support of each observed radial measure, \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) equals \((0,r_*]\) modulo a Lebesgue-null set there, and the separate observed arm limits identify \(\tau_P(x)\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently, under those same radial hypotheses,
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If, in addition, \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains for every sufficiently large \(n\) the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted without that containment, and none is asserted for \(m<q\).  Independently, a law class that contains the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate only when the order-one radial hypotheses and that hard-family containment both hold; for every \(m\geq2\), the faster displayed upper rate is asserted only under the order-\(m\) radial hypotheses, and its matching converse additionally requires contained bumps and \(m\geq q\).

\[

 \qquad H_t=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:(2t-1)u_2>0\}.

\[

 =L^{-1}\int_{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)}

\]

\[

 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n

\]
\[

 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n

\[

 =\begin{cases}

 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)\}

directive:
DIRECTIVE — stat_bdd_uniform_log_penalty v1 (extend D0, then re-run D0.5)

Source verified directly: Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu, arXiv:2510.26051 (CTY_2026_JOE.tex).
Theorem 6 "Distance-based Minimax Convergence Rate" at line 511; the printed
conjecture at line 551. Do not re-fetch or re-derive; the facts below are settled.

Their class P_NP(L,q), verbatim:
 (i)  (Y_i,X_i) i.i.d. in R x R^2.
 (ii) X_i has a Lebesgue density f CONTINUOUS on its compact support X ⊆ [-L,L]^2,
      with L^{-1} <= inf f <= sup f <= L, and B = bd(X) a RECTIFIABLE curve.
 (iii) mu(x)=E[Y|X=x] in a Holder-q ball with constant L.
 (iv) sigma^2(x) continuous with L^{-1} <= sigma^2 <= L.
Their estimator class T = { T_n(U_n(x)) }, U_n(x) = ((Y_i, ||X_i - x||) : i<=n).
Their conclusion: liminf n^{1/4} inf_{T} sup_{P_NP} E[sup_{x in B}|T - mu(x)|] >~ 1,
NO log factor, derived by POINTWISE arguments. Line 551 conjectures the log^{1/4}n
separating this from their (n/log n)^{1/4} uniform upper bound is unimprovable.

=== MUST (easy — corrections, no new mathematics) ===

(1) Delete the "no common modulus" hedge everywhere it appears (honest_scope,
    thm:smooth-geometry-saturation prose, the D0.5 flagship-directive premise).
    CTY condition (ii) requires continuity of each f only; NO modulus uniform across
    n or across a family. The hard family's densities are continuous and inside the
    envelope, so this was never an obstruction.

(2) The coordinatewise decision class is CTY's OWN definition (their T above), not a
    self-imposed restriction. Move that disclosure OUT of technical_internal_limitation
    and INTO the TL;DR, framed as the inherited class. Drop any language suggesting the
    note chose to withhold locations from the estimator.

(3) The density-slack condition is CTY's envelope, not a discovery: floor L^{-1} times
    support area <= 1 forces area <= L, i.e. L >= 4 on [-1,1]^2. State this in ONE
    remark. It is not a headline.

=== MUST (medium — this is the kernel; everything else is secondary) ===

(4) Restate the hard family INSIDE P_NP(L,q) verbatim and prove

      liminf_n (n/log n)^{1/4} inf_{T in T} sup_{P in P_NP} E[ sup_{x in bd(X)} |T - mu(x)| ] >~ 1,

    which settles the conjecture at line 551 same-class.
    Adaptation required: CTY's Theorem 6 targets a SINGLE regression function on the
    boundary of its own support, not a two-arm interface or a treatment-effect
    difference. Recast the angular-cancellation hypercube accordingly; balls now meet
    the support in HALF-discs. The device ports: ∫_0^pi cos(theta) dtheta = 0 keeps the
    radial marginal invariant, and ∫_0^pi cos^2(theta) dtheta = pi/2 != 0 keeps the
    coupling to the affine baseline.
    Verify EACH P_NP condition explicitly for every family member and every n:
    continuity of f; L^{-1} <= f <= L; support ⊆ [-L,L]^2; bd(X) rectifiable;
    mu in the Holder-q ball with constant L; sigma^2 continuous in [L^{-1}, L].
    GUARDRAIL: if some P_NP condition genuinely blocks the family, name WHICH condition
    and STOP. Do NOT retreat to a self-defined class and report an analogue — that
    retreat is the original defect of this note and will be rejected at D0.5.

=== MUST (cut — this costs more score than any missing theorem) ===

(5) Remove the L=4 "elbow" and thm:angular-remainder-transition from the TL;DR and
    project_justification. The elbow is (3). The order-m theorem assumes the radial
    expansion whose failure causes the 1/4 cap and its converse assumes containment of
    the bump submodel used to prove it; keep it as a minor section or drop it. The
    TL;DR must advertise the matched frontier and nothing else.

=== OPTIONAL (do NOT block) ===

(6) The two-arm treatment-effect version (tau = mu_1 - mu_0) inside a CTY-style class.
(7) Restating the smooth-geometry saturation theorem in P_NP.
Record as open-question nodes if they do not fall quickly.

For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the fixed observable radial Radon--Nikodym versions satisfy, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 P\{T=t,\ 0<\lVert X-x\rVert_2\leq r\}
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds,
\]
and agree with the corresponding observed-arm circle integrals for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\).  Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\), so the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) recovers the treatment arm almost surely.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
If zero lies in the essential support of each arm-specific radial measure and the two separate essential limits satisfy \(\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x)\), then
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)
 =\tau_P(x).
\]
In particular, the almost-everywhere radial lower bound and normalized-coarea remainder in \(\mathrm{thm:angular\text{-}remainder\text{-}transition}\) imply these premises arm by arm.

{"id":"thm:straight-information-gap","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  On the nonempty canonical class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\),
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
The location upper bound is attained by the named stabilized bivariate degree-\((q-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) from \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}location\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), with
\[
 h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), normalization, the density floor, and the fixed square support force \(f_P=1/4\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently, for \(q>1\), distance compression has the slower exponent in the strict-slack case \(L>4\); the exponents coincide when \(q=1\), and the no-slack normalization case \(L=4\) coincides for every \(q\).","free_symbols":["\delta","n","q","L","f_P","h","R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{C})","R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal{C})","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}","a_n","s_{n,q}","\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}"],"depends_on":["ass:iid-sampling","ass:deterministic-assignment","ass:consistency","ass:density-envelope","ass:holder-regressions","ass:conditional-subgaussian","ass:straight-half-plane-design","def:observed-assignment-arms","def:distance-decision-class","def:location-decision-class","def:straight-class","def:trimmed-boundary","def:local-constant-estimator","def:triangular-kernel","def:stabilized-distance-local-polynomial","def:stabilized-location-local-polynomial","def:radial-coarea-ambient-class","def:trimmed-distance-risk","def:trimmed-location-risk","def:frontier-rates","lem:density-implies-upper-mass","lem:fixed-local-constant-stability","lem:radial-coarea-identification","lem:stabilized-distance-local-polynomial-admissible","lem:angular-density-packing","lem:coordinatewise-overlap-direct-product"],"proof_tex":"All constants below may depend on the fixed class parameters, \(q\), and \(\delta\), but not on \(n\) or on \(P\).

\emph{Nonemptiness.}  Let \(X\) be uniform on \([-1,1]^2\), use the prescribed two half-planes and chart, take both regressions constant with values in \((1/4,3/4)\), and let each potential outcome be a Bernoulli variable with the corresponding conditional mean plus an independent standard Gaussian variable.  The density \(1/4\) obeys \(L^{-1}\leq 1/4\leq L\).  Each observed arm contains at least a quarter disk at every interface point, so its mass in a radius-\(r\) boundary ball is at least \(\pi r^2/16\), which is no smaller than \(c_-r^2\).  The regressions belong to every displayed H\"older ball after choosing their constant levels inside the envelope.  Finally, Hoeffding's inequality for the centered Bernoulli variable and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\exp\{\lambda(Y(t)-\mu_{t,P}(X))\}\mid X\right]
 \leq \exp(\lambda^2/8)\exp(\lambda^2/2)
 \leq \exp(L^2\lambda^2/2).
\]
Thus this law is in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).

\emph{Full-location upper bound.}  Write \(r_q\), \(K_2\), \(H_t\), and \(G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}location\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\).  If \(v\neq0\), the polynomial \(u\mapsto v^\top r_q(u)\) cannot vanish on the open half-ball \(H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)\).  Therefore
\[
 v^\top G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}v
 =L^{-1}\int_{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)}K_2(u)
 \{v^\top r_q(u)\}^2\,du>0.
\]
Compactness of the unit sphere in this fixed-dimensional coefficient space gives \(\lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}>0\).  The cutoff in the named estimator is consequently well defined.  Its finite sums are Borel, the minimum eigenvalue is continuous on symmetric matrices, and inversion is continuous on the positive-definite cone; hence the cutoff and zero branch make \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) an element of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\).

For \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\) and all sufficiently small \(h\), the rescaled half-ball \(x+h\{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)\}\) lies in the appropriate half-square.  The density floor therefore implies the Loewner inequality
\[
 G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)
 :=\mathbb E_P\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)
 \succeq G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}.
\]
Put
\[
 b_n(h)=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}.
\]
The bounded kernel, bounded monomial vector, density upper bound, and conditional sub-Gaussian inequality imply, entry by entry and for \(0<u\leq1\),
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left(
 \left|\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right|_{ab}>u
 \right)
 \leq2\exp(-cnh^2u^2),
\]
and
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left(
 \left|\widehat r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right|_a>u
 \right)
 \leq2\exp\{-cnh^2\min(u^2,u)\}.
\]
These displays follow by applying the exponential Markov inequality to the centered summands; their conditional variances are at most \(Ch^2\), and the conditional sub-Gaussian premise bounds every higher exponential moment.  Cover the trimmed line segment by a grid of polynomial cardinality in \(n\), apply the union bound to the finitely many matrix and vector entries, and extend from the grid using the Lipschitz kernel and polynomial basis.  On the event \(n^{-1}\sum_i(1+|Y_i|)\leq C\), the extension error is made smaller than \(b_n(h)\) by a sufficiently fine polynomial grid; the complement has polynomially small probability by the same exponential-moment bound.  Thus, uniformly over the class,
\[
 \sup_{t,x}\left\{
 \left\|\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\left\|\widehat r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right\|_2
 \right\}=O_P\{b_n(h)\},
\]
with the same order after taking the expected supremum.

Taylor's formula through total degree \(q-1\), using \(\mu_{t,P}\in\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\), writes
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(x+hu)=r_q(u)^\top\beta_{t,P,x}(h)+R_{t,P,x}(u,h),
 \qquad |R_{t,P,x}(u,h)|\leq Ch^q
\]
on the kernel support.  Polynomial reproduction and the population Gram lower bound show that the population fitted intercept differs from \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) by at most \(Ch^q\).  The Rayleigh-quotient perturbation inequality activates the cutoff whenever the preceding Gram deviation is below \(\lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}/2\) and bounds the inverse there.  On that event, the resolvent identity
\[
 \widehat G^{-1}-G^{-1}
 =\widehat G^{-1}(G-\widehat G)G^{-1}
\]
and the last two displays give stochastic error \(Cb_n(h)\).  On the active branch the cutoff gives \(|\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h}(x)|\leq Ch^{-2}\mathbb P_n|Y|\), while the failed branch is zero.  Cauchy--Schwarz, the uniform second-moment bound implied by conditional sub-Gaussianity, and the polynomially small exceptional probability make the exceptional contribution negligible.  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\{h^q+b_n(h)\}.
\]
For \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), one has \(b_n(h)\leq Ch^q\), proving the upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\) with the named data-driven estimator.

\emph{Full-location converse.}  Work inside the uniform-design submodel just constructed.  Choose \(M\asymp h^{-1}\) trimmed centers with disjoint radius-\(h\) disks.  Keep the control regression and a constant treated baseline fixed.  In alternative \(j\), add
\[
 \Delta\phi((z-x_j)/h),
 \qquad \Delta=\eta h^q,
\]
to the treated regression, where \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_2(0,1))\), \(0\leq\phi\leq1\), and \(\phi(0)=1\).  For every \(k\leq q\),
\[
 \left\|D^k\{\Delta\phi((\cdot-x_j)/h)\}\right\|_\infty
 \leq C\eta h^{q-k}\leq C\eta.
\]
Thus sufficiently small fixed \(\eta\) places every alternative in the same H\"older ball and keeps its Bernoulli probability away from zero and one.  The common Gaussian-noised Bernoulli channel and the bound
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')}
\]
give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq Cn\Delta^2h^2=C\eta^2nh^{2q+2}.
\]
Take \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), with its constant and then \(\eta\) small enough that the last display is at most \(\alpha\log M\) for some \(\alpha<1/4\).  If \(J\) is uniform on the \(M\) alternatives, the log-sum inequality yields
\[
 I(J;O_{1:n})\leq M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
For every decoder, the entropy identity and the binary-error decomposition give
\[
 \Pr(\widehat J\neq J)
 \geq1-\frac{I(J;O_{1:n})+\log2}{\log M}
 \geq c>0
\]
for all large \(n\).  Uniform estimation error smaller than \(\Delta/3\) identifies the unique perturbed center, so Markov's inequality in reverse through this testing reduction gives
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq c\Delta=cs_{n,q}.
\]

\emph{Distance experiment when \(L>4\).}  The canonical exact-distance-regression lemma gives the armwise bias bound \(|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls\).  The fixed local-constant stability lemma gives a population denominator bounded below, and the upper-mass lemma bounds its variance scale by \(Ch^2\).  Repeating the preceding exponential-Markov, boundary-net, and ratio-stability calculation for the fixed triangular-kernel numerator and denominator yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\{h+b_n(h)\}.
\]
At \(h\asymp a_n\), \(b_n(h)\leq Ch\), so the distance upper bound is \(Ca_n\).  For \(L>4\), the canonical-square family in \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\) lies inside \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\); its densities are continuous, although continuity is not required of every member of that class.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\) to its compressed coordinate experiments shows that uniform error below a fixed multiple of \(a_n\) would decode all packed coordinates with probability tending to one, whereas the lemma bounds that success probability by \(1/2+o(1)\).  Hence
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq ca_n.
\]

\emph{Distance experiment when \(L=4\).}  The fixed square has Lebesgue area four, the score law has total mass one, and the density floor is \(1/4\).  Therefore
\[
 0=1-\int_{[-1,1]^2}\frac14\,dz
 =\int_{[-1,1]^2}\left\{f_P(z)-\frac14\right\}\,dz.
\]
The integrand is nonnegative Lebesgue-almost everywhere, so
\[
 f_P(z)=\frac14
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }z\in[-1,1]^2.
\]
No continuity is used.  This almost-everywhere equality suffices for every expectation and risk because densities differing on a null set induce the same score law.  It also suffices for the fixed radial Radon--Nikodym versions: polar Fubini implies that, for each trimmed \(x\), the circle integral sees the null exceptional set at only a Lebesgue-null set of radii.  Consequently, for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small \(s\),
\[
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\frac{\pi}{4}s.
\]
Thus all expectations, Radon--Nikodym identities, circle identities, and risk bounds used below are unchanged by replacing \(f_P\) with its constant representative \(1/4\).

Taylor expansion of \(\mu_{t,P}\) through total degree \(q-1\), followed by integration over the appropriate half-circle and division by \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\), supplies uniformly bounded coefficients \(b_{t,k,P}(x)\) such that
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{q-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|
 \leq Cs^q
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  This uses only the H\"older remainder \(Cs^q\); the half-circle moments of each Taylor monomial produce the displayed polynomial coefficients.

Instantiate \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) with \(m=q\) and cutoff constant \(c=\pi/4\).  Its population radial Gram matrix is
\[
 \frac1{h^2}\int_0^h K_\triangle(s/h)v_q(s/h)v_q(s/h)^\top
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
 =\frac\pi4 G_q,
\]
where equality holds because changing an integrand on a null set does not change the integral.  The matrix \(G_q\) is positive definite: for \(v\neq0\), the nonzero polynomial \(v^\top v_q(u)\) has only finitely many zeros, while \(uK_\triangle(u)>0\) on \((0,1)\).  The established admissibility lemma places this estimator in \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  The same entrywise exponential inequalities, now for the radial polynomial basis, the same boundary net, polynomial reproduction, and the preceding remainder yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(q),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\{h^q+b_n(h)\}.
\]
At \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), this is at most \(Cs_{n,q}\).

Every coordinatewise distance rule can be implemented from the full sample and known geometry by computing \(D_{P,x,i}\) from \((X_i,T_i)\).  Hence \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) is a restriction of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\), and, for the common loss and law class,
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq cs_{n,q}.
\]
This proves the \(L=4\) distance equivalence.  Finally,
\[
 \frac{q}{2q+2}>\frac14
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q>1.
\]
Thus the strict-slack distance exponent is slower exactly when \(q>1\), the exponents agree at \(q=1\), and the no-slack case agrees for every \(q\), as claimed.","status":"proved","justification":"Holding geometry and the causal target fixed reveals the statistical price of releasing only one distance coordinate, and also identifies the no-density-slack exception.","gap":"The full-regressor benchmark and location-based boundary theory do not pair their rate with a direct distance-only angular-confounding converse on the identical straight class.","consumer":"A data steward can determine whether a distance-only release loses an exponent: it does for \(q>1\) only when \(L>4\), and it does not when \(L=4\)."}
