{"id":"thm:angular-remainder-transition","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  This is a conditional risk-transfer theorem.  Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be a subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
\]
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|
 \leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Under exactly these radial hypotheses, zero lies in the essential support of each observed radial measure, \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) equals \((0,r_*]\) modulo a Lebesgue-null set there, and the separate observed arm limits identify \(\tau_P(x)\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently, under those same radial hypotheses,
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If, in addition, \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains for every sufficiently large \(n\) the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted without that containment, and none is asserted for \(m<q\).  Independently, a law class that contains the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate only when the order-one radial hypotheses and that hard-family containment both hold; for every \(m\geq2\), the faster displayed upper rate is asserted only under the order-\(m\) radial hypotheses, and its matching converse additionally requires contained bumps and \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that, for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small treated-half-circle radius, a locally constant regression gives a constant normalized-coarea ratio, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives the ratio \(s^{1+\alpha}/2\) for some \(0<\alpha<1\) and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder even in the almost-everywhere sense.  Hence density alone does not determine these examples' joint normalized-coarea remainder; no universal weakest-threshold impossibility is asserted.","free_symbols":["m","q","\iota","n","t","s","P","L","\delta","\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{coarea}}","\mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}","Q_{t,P,x}","N_{t,P,x}","g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}","\mathcal{S}_{t,P,x}","\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}","\mu_{t,P}","\tau_P","R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{C})","\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{dist}}_n","K_\triangle","h","a_n","\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}","f_P","\widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}"],"depends_on":["ass:iid-sampling","ass:deterministic-assignment","ass:consistency","ass:assignment-partition","ass:compact-support","ass:score-absolute-continuity","ass:holder-regressions","ass:conditional-subgaussian","ass:smooth-embedding","def:observed-assignment-arms","def:circle-density-integral","def:circle-outcome-integral","def:positive-q-radius-domain","def:canonical-distance-regression","def:observed-distance-arm-limit","def:signed-distance","def:radial-coarea-ambient-class","def:trimmed-boundary","def:triangular-kernel","def:stabilized-distance-local-polynomial","def:trimmed-distance-risk","def:frontier-rates","def:angular-density-handle","lem:radial-coarea-identification","lem:angular-density-packing","lem:coordinatewise-overlap-direct-product","lem:stabilized-distance-local-polynomial-admissible"],"status":"to-prove","proof_tex":"All constants below may depend on \(m,q,\iota,L,\delta,A,r_*,\underline c,\overline c\), and the common coefficient bound, but not on \(n\), \(P\), \(t\), or \(x\).  We take the cutoff input suppressed in \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) to be \(c=\underline c\), and take \(h\leq r_*\).

First, the lower radial inequality gives
\[
 \int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\geq\frac{\underline c}{2}r^2>0,
 \qquad 0<r\leq r_*.
\]
It also gives \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\), so \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) equals that interval modulo a null set.  If \(B\) is the common coefficient bound, then the remainder assumption implies
\[
 |g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 \leq B\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}s^k+As^m\longrightarrow0
\]
for almost every such \(s\downarrow0\).  The radial-coarea identification lemma therefore proves the separate essential limits and
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]

We next prove the uniform upper bound.  Put \(v(u)=v_m(u)\), \(G=G_m\), and \(S_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2\).  The arm-specific population matrices and vectors corresponding to the estimator are
\[
 \overline G_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\frac1{h^2}\int_0^hK_\triangle(s/h)v(s/h)v(s/h)^\top
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
\]
and
\[
 \overline r_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\frac1{h^2}\int_{\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\cap(0,h)}
 K_\triangle(s/h)v(s/h)
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
The assumed radial lower bound gives \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,h)\), so the complement of \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\cap(0,h)\) in \((0,h)\) is Lebesgue-null.  By the Radon--Nikodym identities defining \(N_{t,P,x}\) and \(Q_{t,P,x}\), the restricted integral is therefore exactly the population outcome vector corresponding to the estimator.  In particular, no value of the partial regression is used outside \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\).  Changing variables \(s=hu\) and using the almost-everywhere radial bounds gives, in Loewner order,
\[
 \underline cG\preceq\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)
 \preceq\overline cG.
\]
The matrix \(G\) is positive definite: if \(a\neq0\), the polynomial \(a^\top v(u)\) is not zero almost everywhere on \((0,1)\), and hence
\[
 a^\top Ga=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)\{a^\top v(u)\}^2\,du>0.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_{\min}(\overline G_{t,P,x}(h))\geq\underline c\lambda_{\min}(G)\), exactly the population margin used by the declared cutoff.

Define
\[
 \beta_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\bigl(\mu_{t,P}(x),b_{t,1,P}(x)h,\ldots,
 b_{t,m-1,P}(x)h^{m-1}\bigr)^\top.
\]
The polynomial part of the radial expansion equals \(v(s/h)^\top\beta_{t,P,x}(h)\).  Consequently,
\[
 \overline r_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)\beta_{t,P,x}(h)+e_{t,P,x}(h),
\]
where, since \(\lVert v(u)\rVert_2\leq\sqrt m\) on \([0,1]\),
\[
 \lVert e_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert_2
 \leq\frac{A\overline c\sqrt m}{h^2}
 \int_0^h s^{m+1}\,ds
 \leq C h^m.
\]
It follows that the population fitted intercept obeys
\[
 \left|e_1^\top\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)^{-1}
 \overline r_{t,P,x}(h)-\mu_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \leq Ch^m.
\]
This calculation uses only almost-everywhere radial identities; changing a Radon--Nikodym representative on a null set changes none of the integrals.

For completeness, we derive the stochastic order.  For a fixed \(t,x\), each entry of the empirical Gram summand is bounded by \(Ch^{-2}\), and the upper radial inequality gives
\[
 P\{T=t,\ S_x\leq h\}=\int_0^hQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
 \leq\frac{\overline c}{2}h^2.
\]
Hence its variance is at most \(Ch^{-2}\).  Conditional sub-Gaussianity, consistency, and the H\"older-ball supremum bound similarly imply, for every integer \(k\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left|
 h^{-2}\mathbf1\{T=t\}K_\triangle(S_x/h)v_j(S_x/h)Y
 \right|^k
 \leq k!C^kh^{2-2k}.
\]
Centering changes only the constant.  Expanding the exponential series and applying exponential Markov inequality therefore gives, for every scalar Gram or outcome coordinate \(Z_{t,x,h}\),
\[
 P\!\left(\left|(\mathbb P_n-P)Z_{t,x,h}\right|>u\right)
 \leq2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{cnu^2}{h^{-2}+h^{-2}u}\right\}.
\]

The smooth embedded boundary is contained in \([-L,L]^2\).  For \(\epsilon_n=n^{-4}\), it has an \(\epsilon_n\)-net of cardinality at most \(C_Ln^8\), obtained from the ambient square.  A \(C^1\) image of a compact interval is planar-null, so score absolute continuity implies that, with probability one, no sample score lies on \(\mathcal B_P\).  Therefore the strict sign in the estimator equals \(\mathbf1\{T_i=t\}\) simultaneously for every boundary point and sample index.  On \([0,1]\), the finitely many functions
\[
 u\longmapsto K_\triangle(u)v_j(u),
 \qquad
 u\longmapsto K_\triangle(u)v_j(u)v_k(u)
\]
are Lipschitz.  Reverse triangle inequality consequently bounds empirical oscillations between a boundary point and its net point by
\[
 C_m\epsilon_nh^{-3}
 \quad\text{for Gram entries},
 \qquad
 C_m\epsilon_nh^{-3}\mathbb P_n|Y|
 \quad\text{for outcome coordinates},
\]
with the same population bounds.  The conditional tail envelope gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P(\mathbb P_n|Y|)^2\leq C,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\max_{i\leq n}|Y_i|^2\leq C\log n.
\]
A union bound over the fixed matrix dimension, the two arms, and the polynomial net shows that, for every fixed \(A_0>0\), an event \(\mathcal G_n\) of probability at least \(1-Cn^{-A_0}\) exists on which
\[
 \sup_{P,t,x}\left\{
 \lVert\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)-\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\lVert\widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)-\overline r_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert_2
 \right\}
 \leq C\eta_n(h),
\]
where
\[
 \eta_n(h)=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}.
\]
Here and below the supremum notation means that the same constants and probability bound hold uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal C\), not that samples under different laws share one probability space.

For \(h=h_n\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2m+2)}\), \(\eta_n(h_n)\to0\).  Weyl's eigenvalue inequality and the population margin imply on \(\mathcal G_n\), for all large \(n\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h_n))
 \geq\frac12\underline c\lambda_{\min}(G).
\]
Thus every cutoff is active and every empirical inverse is uniformly bounded.  The coefficient vector \(\beta_{t,P,x}(h_n)\) is uniformly bounded, so the inverse identity
\[
 \widehat G^{-1}-\overline G^{-1}
 =\widehat G^{-1}(\overline G-\widehat G)\overline G^{-1}
\]
and the preceding population bias yield
\[
 \sup_{t,x}
 |\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h_n,\underline c}(x)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 \leq C\{h_n^m+\eta_n(h_n)\}
\]
on \(\mathcal G_n\).  On its complement, the admissibility lemma gives
\[
 |\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h_n,\underline c}(x)|
 \leq Ch_n^{-2}\mathbb P_n|Y|,
\]
with zero on the failed-cutoff branch.  Cauchy--Schwarz and the arbitrarily large polynomial exponent \(A_0\) make the exceptional expected contribution \(o(h_n^m)\).  The admissibility lemma also proves that the arm difference belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  Since
\[
 h_n^m\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh_n^2}}\asymp h_n^m,
 \qquad
 \frac{\log n}{nh_n^2}\asymp h_n^{2m},
\]
we obtain
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Taking the infimum over the distance decision class proves the asserted risk upper bound.

We now verify the conditional converse.  Work on the uniform square \([-1/2,1/2]^2\) with the horizontal straight interface, and choose \(M\asymp h_n^{-1}\) trimmed centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) whose radius-\(h_n\) disks are disjoint.  Let \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_2(0,1))\) be radial with \(\phi(0)=1\), put \(\Delta_n=\eta h_n^m\), and keep the control regression zero.  Under the baseline the treated regression is zero, while under alternative \(j\) it is
\[
 \mu_{1,j}(z)=\Delta_n\phi((z-x_j)/h_n).
\]
Take independent standard Gaussian errors in both potential outcomes.  For every derivative order \(k\leq q\),
\[
 \lVert D^k\mu_{1,j}\rVert_\infty
 \leq C\eta h_n^{m-k}\leq C\eta
\]
because \(m\geq q\) and \(h_n\leq1\).  Thus sufficiently small fixed \(\eta\) puts every law in the ambient \(q\)-H\"older and conditional sub-Gaussian class.  In fact the scaled bumps have all derivatives through order \(m\) uniformly bounded, so Taylor's formula and half-circle averaging verify the order-\(m\) normalized-coarea remainder uniformly at every trimmed boundary point.  Uniform design gives \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\pi s\) for all sufficiently small relevant radii.  Hence these are precisely valid contained bump laws of the kind stipulated by the theorem; the extra containment hypothesis places them in \(\mathcal C\).

For the observed full sample, Gaussian relative entropy and the area of a bump support give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac n2\mathbb E\!\left[
 \mathbf1\{T=1\}\mu_{1,j}(X)^2\right]
 \leq Cn\Delta_n^2h_n^2
 =C\eta^2nh_n^{2m+2}.
\]
Now \(nh_n^{2m+2}\asymp\log n\) and \(\log M\sim(2m+2)^{-1}\log n\).  Decreasing \(\eta\) makes the last divergence at most \(\alpha\log M\) for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\).  If \(J\) is uniform on \(\{0,1,\ldots,M\}\), the log-sum inequality gives
\[
 I(J;O_{1:n})
 \leq\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
For any decoder \(\widehat J\), writing \(E=\mathbf1\{\widehat J\neq J\}\) and expanding conditional entropy gives
\[
 H(J\mid O_{1:n})\leq H(E)+P(E)\log M
 \leq\log2+P(E)\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\), the preceding two displays bound \(P(E)\) away from zero.  Uniform estimation error below \(\Delta_n/3\) identifies whether there is no bump or which unique center carries the bump.  Therefore even the full-location minimax risk, and hence the distance-only risk, is at least
\[
 c\Delta_n
 =c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
This proves exactness under the stated containment and \(m\geq q\).  When either condition is absent, this construction supplies no same-class converse, exactly as the theorem records.

Independently, suppose a law class contains the shrinking angular-imbalance hypercube from \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\).  Its separated centers, adjacent compressed divergences, and target gap are those of the angular-density packing lemma.  Given an arbitrary fixed-\(n\) coordinatewise rule, first induce a marked-Poisson rule by retaining the \(n\) smallest-mark observations on \(\{N\geq n\}\), applying the fixed-\(n\) rule there, and using the zero default otherwise.  The retained observations are independent with the original law.  The disjoint bump-cell restrictions of the marked Poisson process are conditionally independent, and midpoint thresholding the induced rule gives the decentralized decoders of the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma.  The packing slack keeps their Poisson divergences below \(2\alpha\log M_n\) with \(2\alpha<1\), so the probability of at least one error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).  Error below half the target separation would decode every bit.  Since \(P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\leq e^{-cn}\) and the zero-default target loss is uniformly bounded on the hard family, the induced Poisson risk is at most the fixed-\(n\) risk plus \(O(e^{-cn})\).  Thus that class has distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  For \(m=1\), the upper exponent is \(1/4\); for \(m\geq2\), the displayed conditional upper exponent is strictly larger.  The converse statements remain limited to the two explicitly contained hard families.

It remains to prove the density example.  Fix \(0<\alpha<1\), take the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\) with horizontal interface through the origin, and define
\[
 f(z)=
 \begin{cases}
 1+\lVert z\rVert_2^{\alpha-1}z_1,&z\neq0,\\
 1,&z=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Because \(|\lVert z\rVert_2^{\alpha-1}z_1|\leq\lVert z\rVert_2^\alpha<1\) on \(S\), this density is bounded, positive, and continuous.  Its second term is odd in \(z_1\), so its integral over \(S\) is zero; since \(S\) has area one, \(f\) integrates to one.  On a treated half-circle of radius \(0<s<1/2\), write \(z=s(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), \(0\leq\theta\leq\pi\).  Then
\[
 f(z)=1+s^\alpha\cos\theta,
 \qquad
 Q_{1,P,0}(s)=s\int_0^\pi(1+s^\alpha\cos\theta)\,d\theta=\pi s.
\]
For a constant regression \(\mu(z)=c\), the radial ratio is identically \(c\).  For the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\), it is instead
\[
\begin{aligned}
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,0}(s)
 &=\frac{s\int_0^\pi s\cos\theta
 (1+s^\alpha\cos\theta)\,d\theta}{\pi s}\\
 &=\frac{s^{1+\alpha}}2.
\end{aligned}
\]
If an order-two expansion existed, some constant \(b_1\) and finite \(A\) would satisfy
\[
 \left|\frac{s^{1+\alpha}}2-b_1s\right|\leq As^2
\]
for almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  Dividing first by \(s\) and sending \(s\downarrow0\) forces \(b_1=0\); dividing then by \(s^2\) would require \(s^{\alpha-1}/2\leq A\), which is impossible because \(\alpha<1\).  Thus the same bounded positive continuous density supports a constant-regression example with an exact constant ratio and an affine-regression example that fails the order-two remainder.  This proves the final claim without asserting any universal weakest density threshold."}

{"id":"def:stabilized-distance-local-polynomial","name":"\widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}","construction":"Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), a cutoff constant \(c>0\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Put \(v_m(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{m-1})^\top\), let \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), and set \(S_{P,x,i}=|D_{P,x,i}|\).  At the probability-zero value \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), assign the observation to neither arm.  Define
\[
 \widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
Let
\[
 G_m=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad \lambda_m(c)=c\lambda_{\min}(G_m),
\]
and define the stabilized arm intercept and arm difference by
\[
 \widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}

 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}<\lambda_m(c)/2,

 -\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{0,h,c}(x).
\]
The cutoff input \(c\) is suppressed from the notation for \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\).  The formula is defined for every \(h>0\); in an order-\(m\) coarea class it is used with \(c=\underline c\) and \(0<h\leq r_*\). Every law has support \(S\), a continuous density \(f_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq f_{P_\omega}\leq L\), a regression \(\mu_{P_\omega}\) in the stated \(q\)-H\"older ball, and a continuous conditional variance \(\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\leq L\).  The boundary \(\operatorname{bd}(S)\) is rectifiable and the observations are independently and identically distributed.  If \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs from \(\omega\) only in coordinate \(j\), then

\[

\[

\]
If \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs from \(\omega\) only in coordinate \(j\), then the laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree, the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and

Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}
 \geq\frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]
Along any sequence with \(M=M_n\to\infty\) and fixed \(\kappa<1\), this lower bound is \(1/2-o(1)\).

\[

\[

{"id":"def:cty-a1-a2-class","name":"\mathcal{P}_{12}","construction":"For integers \(p\geq1\), real numbers \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), let \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) be the set of laws \(P\) satisfying all the following member properties.

\(\mathrm{(i)}\) For every \(n\), the vectors \((Y_i(0),Y_i(1),X_i)\), \(1\leq i\leq n\), are independently and identically distributed; \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_{1,P}\}\); and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

\(\mathrm{(ii)}\) The support has the CTY rectangular form \(\mathcal X_P=[\underline x_P,\overline x_P]^2\subseteq[-L,L]^2\).  The variable \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\), such that \(L^{-1}\leq f_P(x)\leq L\) for all \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

\(\mathrm{(iii)}\) For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mu_{t,P}(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]\) has a \(C^{p+1}\) extension to an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal X_P\), and
\[
 \max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}|\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 +\max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\neq z\in\mathcal X_P}
 { |\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)-\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(z)|\over\lVert x-z\rVert_2}
 \leq L.
\]

\(\mathrm{(iv)}\) For each \(t\), \(\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(t)\mid X=x)\) is continuous and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)\leq L\) on \(\mathcal X_P\).

\(\mathrm{(v)}\) For each \(t\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^{2+\nu}\mid X=x]\leq L.
\]

\(\mathrm{(vi)}\) The sets \(\mathcal A_{0,P}\) and \(\mathcal A_{1,P}\) form a Borel partition of \(\mathcal X_P\), and their known common interface \(\mathcal B_P\subset\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a compact rectifiable curve satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\leq L\).

\(\mathrm{(vii)}\) The known metric is exactly Euclidean, \(d_P(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\), and the known kernel is \(K_\square\).  The collection
\[
 \{\{z\in\mathcal X_P:\lVert z-x\rVert_2\leq r\}:x\in\mathcal X_P, r\geq0\}
\]
is a VC class with VC index at most four.

\(\mathrm{(viii)}\) Put \(r_p(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(I_1=[0,\infty)\), \(I_0=(-\infty,0)\), and
\[
 \Psi_{t,P,x}(h)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 {1\over h^2}\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)^\top
 \right].
\]
For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\Psi_{t,P,x}(h))\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(ix)}\) For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\),
\[
 {1\over h^2}\int_{\mathcal A_{t,P}}
 K_\square(\{(2t-1)\lVert z-x\rVert_2\}/h)\,dz\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(x)}\) For every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), both \(t\), and every \(0<s\leq L^{-1}\), the one-dimensional Hausdorff integral of \(f_P\) over
\[
 \{z\in\mathcal A_{t,P}:\lVert z-x\rVert_2=s\}
\]
is finite and strictly positive.

These clauses are the exact \(L\)-uniformized conditions from CTY Assumptions~1--2 and Theorem~2 used below.  In particular, clause \(\mathrm{(v)}\) is the raw conditional-moment envelope, and clause \(\mathrm{(vii)}\) retains the uniform-kernel VC requirement in Assumption~2(iii).","free_symbols":["n","p","\nu","L","P","T","Y","Y(t)","X","\mathcal{X}_P","f_P","\mu_{t,P}","\sigma^2_{t,P}","\mathcal{A}_{t,P}","\mathcal{B}_P","d_P","K_\square","r_p","D^{\pm}_{P,x}","\Psi_{t,P,x}(h)","\mathcal{P}_{12}","h"],"inputs":["def:cty-uniform-kernel","def:cty-known-geometry","def:cty-known-geometry-signed-distance-data"]}

The note has two distinct, non-substitutable statistical functionals.  First, for \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), the causal target is the boundary treatment-effect curve \(\tau_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Under CTY Theorem~1 it equals the difference of the two one-sided signed-distance conditional-mean limits.  The estimator observes \(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n)\), may use the known geometry \(G_P\), and belongs to the law-independent sectionwise-Borel class \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\).  Its explicit outer-expectation minimax functional is
\[
 R_n^{12,\pm}(p,\nu,L)=\inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right].
\]
For \(q=p+1\geq2\), this risk is of exact order \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) when \(\nu>2\), with the stabilized degree-\(p\) signed-distance local-polynomial rule as an explicit upper witness; at \(\nu=2\) the proved upper rate is \(n^{-1/4}(\log n)^{1/3}\).

Second, and unchanged from the accepted checkpoint, for each \(x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) the observed input is \(V_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n)\).  The enlarged point-indexed class \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) consists of all law-independent families \(\{T_{n,x}:x\in\mathbb R^2\}\) whose fixed-\(x\) sections are Borel and whose output is \(T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))\).  Its outer-expectation risk is \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\).  The preserved theorem proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) on the full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), and strict inclusion yields the inherited CTY common-map converse.  No full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper theorem is claimed.

Let \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), \(L\geq4\), \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), and \(B\geq1\).  Let \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\) solve the original, unwinsorized population normal equations, and define
\[
 \widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)={1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 \left[\psi_B(Y_i)-r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\right].
\]
There is a constant \(C=C(p,L)\) such that
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{t\in\{0,1\},\,x\in\mathcal B_P}
 \left\|\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)-\mathbb E_P\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)\right\|
 \right]
 \leq C\left\{
 \sqrt{{\log(1/h)\over nh^2}}+{B\log(1/h)\over nh^2}
 \right\}
\]
whenever \(h\downarrow0\) and \(nh^2/\log(1/h)\to\infty\).  This is a direct bounded-envelope adaptation of the expected maximal-inequality proof in Supplemental Appendix SA-6.2--SA-6.4 of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, not a verbatim theorem attributed to them.

\[

\]

\[

The note has two distinct, non-substitutable statistical functionals.  First, for \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), where \(p\geq0\), \(q=p+1\geq1\), and \(\nu\geq2\), the causal target is \(\tau_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Under CTY Theorem~1 it equals the difference of the two one-sided signed-distance conditional-mean limits.  The estimator observes \(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n)\), may use the known geometry \(G_P\), and belongs to the law-independent sectionwise-Borel class \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\).  Its outer-expectation minimax functional is
\[
 R_n^{12,\pm}(p,\nu,L)=\inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right].
\]
On the exact displayed \(L\)-uniformized Euclidean-distance, uniform-kernel CTY Assumptions~1--2 plus Theorem-2-envelope class, this risk is of exact order \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) for every \(p\geq0\) and \(\nu\geq2\).  The attaining witness is the explicit winsorized, Gram-stabilized degree-\(p\) signed-distance local-polynomial estimator with \(h_n=a_n\), \(\psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}\), and \(B_n=a_n^{-1/3}\).

Second, for each \(x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\), the observed input is \(V_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n)\).  The enlarged class \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) contains all law-independent point-indexed families whose fixed-\(x\) sections are Borel.  The preserved theorem proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) on the full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), and strict inclusion yields the inherited CTY common-map converse.  No full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper theorem is claimed.

changed.to:
Fix an integer \(p\geq0\), a number \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\).  For \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(h>0\), let \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\in\mathbb R^{p+1}\) solve the original, unwinsorized population normal equations
\[
 \Psi_{t,P,x}(h)\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 {1\over h^2}\mathbf1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)Y
 \right],
\]
and put \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\).  There is a constant \(C=C(p,L)<\infty\) such that, for every deterministic sequence \((h_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfying \(h_n>0\), \(h_n\downarrow0\), and \(nh_n^2\to\infty\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 \left|
 e_1^\top\{\beta^*_{1,P,x}(h_n)-\beta^*_{0,P,x}(h_n)\}-\tau_P(x)
 \right|
 \leq Ch_n.
\]
changed.reason: CTY Theorem~2 states its uniform first-order contrast-bias conclusion only along deterministic bandwidth sequences with \(h_n\downarrow0\) and \(nh_n^2\to\infty\).  The current unqualified interface omits both source hypotheses and also describes an armwise conclusion not needed downstream; the proposed claim records exactly the contrast conclusion used by the upper proposition.

First, for \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), where \(p\geq0\), \(q=p+1\geq1\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), the causal target is \(\tau_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Under CTY Theorem~1 it equals the difference of the two one-sided signed-distance conditional-mean limits.  The estimator observes \(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n)\), may use the known geometry \(G_P\), and belongs to the law-independent sectionwise-Borel class \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\).  Its outer-expectation minimax functional is
\[
 R_n^{12,\pm}(p,\nu,L)=\inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right].
\]
The explicit winsorized, Gram-stabilized degree-\(p\) signed-distance local-polynomial estimator with \(h_n=a_n\), \(\psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}\), and \(B_n=a_n^{-1/3}\) attains the upper rate \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) for every \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\).  The exact matched two-sided rate holds for every \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq L_0(p)\).

Second, for each \(x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\), the observed input is \(V_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n)\).  The enlarged class \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) contains all law-independent point-indexed families whose fixed-\(x\) sections are Borel.  The preserved theorem proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) on the full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).  It strictly enlarges the literal common-map class displayed by CTY, \(\mathcal T=\{T_n(U_n(x)):T_n\in\mathcal T_n\}\), and strict inclusion yields the converse for that literal displayed class.  Here ``same-class'' refers to the same \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) law class.  No full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper theorem is claimed.

The note has two distinct, non-substitutable statistical functionals.  First, for each \(x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\), the observed input is \(V_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n)\).  The enlarged class \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) contains all law-independent point-indexed families whose fixed-\(x\) sections are Borel.  The first co-main theorem proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) on the full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) class for integer \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\).  This class strictly enlarges the literal common-map class displayed by CTY, \(\mathcal T=\{T_n(U_n(x)):T_n\in\mathcal T_n\}\), so inclusion gives the common-map converse on the same law class.  This contribution is converse-only and supplies no full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper theorem.

Second, for \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), where \(p\geq0\), \(q=p+1\geq1\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), the causal target is \(\tau_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Under CTY Theorem~1 it equals the difference of the two one-sided signed-distance conditional-mean limits.  The estimator observes \(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n)\), may use the known geometry \(G_P\), and belongs to the law-independent sectionwise-Borel class \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\).  Its outer-expectation minimax functional is
\[
 R_n^{12,\pm}(p,\nu,L)=\inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right].
\]
The explicit winsorized, Gram-stabilized degree-\(p\) signed-distance local-polynomial estimator with \(h_n=a_n\), \(\psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}\), and \(B_n=a_n^{-1/3}\) attains the upper rate \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) for every \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\).  The fixed-known-interior-boundary converse over arbitrary known-geometry point-indexed Borel sections gives the matching lower rate when \(L\geq L_0(p)\).  Hence the exact matched outer-expected rate holds on this one common \(\mathcal P_{12}\) law, risk, and decision triple, not on all of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\).
